cases.question: What is the formal procedure for reporting workplace bullying or harassment?
cases.answer: According to section 2.2.3 of the HR Policy (page 11), staff members are encouraged to report incidents of workplace bullying or harassment to their immediate Manager, a Senior Manager, or the CEO. If the complaint is against the CEO, it may be made to the Board. The Manager or Senior Manager should then report the incident to the Manager: Finance and Operations and/or the CEO, so that an investigation can be commenced where appropriate.

According to section 2.2.3 of the HR Policy (document [1]), any employee who believes that conduct in violation of the sexual harassment policy may be occurring or may have occurred is urged and expected to report the relevant facts immediately to their Managers, to the senior management or the CEO or the Board (as the case may be). 

Additionally, section 9.1 of the HR Policy (document [2]) states that complaints of alleged violations of established policies and practices, including workplace bullying or harassment, should be addressed through the grievance procedure.

The formal procedure for reporting workplace bullying or harassment is outlined in section 9.1.1 of the HR Policy (document [3]), which states that staff members are encouraged to begin the grievance procedure by discussing the problem orally with their immediate Manager. The Manager should make a reasonable effort to resolve the issue expeditiously and in any event within 30 days of the issue being reported.

It's also worth noting that section 9.6 of the HR Policy (document [4]) states that a person who has reported suspected misconduct shall not be subject to any detrimental treatment as a result of reporting the misconduct, and that any complaint of retaliation will be investigated and considered gross misconduct.

cases.question: What are the core responsibilities of the Human Resources Manager?
cases.answer:
The core responsibilities of the Human Resources Manager include:

* initiating and developing human resource policies, procedures, and practices [3]
* implementing and monitoring human resource policies and procedures as contained in the Manual [3]
* facilitating the recruitment and hiring of staff [3]
* providing fair and equitable compensation based on job demand and regular appraisal of an individual’s performance [3]
* advising management on all human resource matters [3]
* facilitating the achievement of a working environment which encourages staff development, motivation, and enhances the personal dignity of staff members [3]
* co-ordinating the preparation of annual leave programme [3]
* advising Management on matters relating to discipline and the procedures to be followed in handling disciplinary cases [3]
* being the custodian of the Manual and initiating regular reviews of the same [3]

cases.question: What are the rules and eligibility criteria for working from home?
cases.answer: According to section 8.6 of the HRPolicy.pdf (page 57), staff members can work from home with GESCI's consent, and their home is considered a location of work subject to the OSHA. To work from home, staff members must be aware that authorized occupational safety and health officers can visit their home-based office, and GESCI reserves the right to inspect their home-working environment to ensure health and safety standards are met. cases.question: What are the standard daily working hours and lunch break provisions?
cases.answer: The standard daily working hours are 9.00 am to 5:30 pm, Monday to Friday [1]. Staff members are also required to take one hour for lunch [1].

cases.question: How many days of annual leave can an employee carry over to the following year?
cases.answer: According to [1], staff members can carry forward up to 5 days of their annual leave entitlement beyond December 31, with the consent of the CEO. Any approved days carried forward must be taken by 30th June the following year.
